verdict.rationale: PlayCanvas documents built-in physics through components: rigidbody, collision and joint components, powered by ammo.js (a WebAssembly port of Bullet). These components are available across the Editor, the standalone Engine, React and Web Components. Missing for 10: any evidence of raycast support, confirmation that the ammo.js module is included out of the box without extra setup, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a game developer, built-in physics — rigid bodies, collisions, raycasts — works out of the box

citations.quote: The rigidbody component decides how an entity moves, the collision component gives it a physical shape, and the alpha joint component constrains bodies to one another.
PlayCanvas physics is powered by ammo.js, a WebAssembly port of the open source Bullet physics engine. You work with it through components.
The same components, with the same properties, are available whichever way you build: in the Editor, directly against the engine, in PlayCanvas React and in Web Components.
